newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Poll shows Belgian governing parties waning.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Belgian governing parties waning.

text.p: The four parties making up Belgium's governing centre-left coalition, beset by scandals, are starting to pay the price among the electorate, according to an opinion poll in Monday's La Libre Belgique newspaper.

The face-to-face poll of 2,000 people between December 2 and December 12 shows the francophone Socialist Party getting 30.5 percent of the vote against 31.7 percent in a similar poll in September and 33.8 percent at the national election in May 1995.
Its sister Flemish Socialist Party's share of the vote has likewise fallen to 10.8 percent from 18.2 in September and 19.9 percent at the election.
The Flemish Christian Democratic Party, the largest in the coalition and of which Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene is a member, has also lost ground.
Its share of the vote has dropped to 25.8 percent from 26.5 in September and 27.3 percent in May 1995.
The share going to its sister francophone Christian Democratic Party has also slid to 18.7 percent from 19.1 in September and 22.7 percent at the election.

In August that police rescued two young sexually-abused girls from makeshift dungeon in a house owned by convicted paedophile rapist Marc Dutroux and later unearthed the bodies of four more. Dutroux and four others are still in jail.

Two months later more than 250,000 people marched through Brussels in a demonstration both of support for the victims and their families and of disgust at what is widely seen as an inefficient and corrupt political and legal system.
Earlier this month Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo was cleared by parliament of a series of allegations he had indulged in sex with boys under the legal age of consent of 16 years.
The allegations revealed deep rifts within the government, and political sources said the issue was only resolved when Di Rupo's francophone socialists threatened to quit the coalition.
Jean-Pierre Grafe, a Christian Democratic minister in the country's Walloon regional government, resigned in the face of allegations he had indulged in under-age sex.
He said he was innocent but could not continue to carry out his ministerial duties in the over-heated climate.

Alain Van Der Biest, a former francophone Socialist federal and regional minister, was arrested in September in connection with the 1991 assassination of Socialist Party patriarch Andre Cools. He is still in prison while enquiries continue.
Other scandals ranging from allegations of tax evasion to misuse of funds have discredited several other federal and regional government members.
Meanwhile the francophone and Flemish Liberal Parties, the main opposition in the parliament, have been moving only gradually up the opinion polls.
The Libre Belgique poll shows the francophone Liberals getting 28.8 percent of the vote against 28.2 percent in September and 22.7 percent in the May 1995 elections.
Its sister Flemish Liberal Party's share of the vote has risen to 22.8 percent from 22.1 in September and 20.7 at the elections.
A national election is not due until 1999.
